policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'These things spake Jesus' renders the name alike with or without the article; English carries no trace of ho.

ASV 'and lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said' is a participle plus finite verb, not the finite pair 'he lifted up his eyes and said'; that excludes r02 (eperen ... kai eipen) but base and r01 are the same participial text and English cannot separate them.
ASV 'that the Son may glorify thee' has no 'also'; ASV renders an adverbial kai in such a hina clause with 'also', so the bare hina stands.
ASV shifts from 'thy Son' in the first clause to 'the Son' in the second; the possessive sou is absent from the English exactly where it would have been rendered 'thy'.
ASV 'he should give eternal life' renders the hina clause the same whether the verb is aorist subjunctive or future indicative.
ASV 'I glorified thee on the earth, having accomplished the work' subordinates the second verb as a participle; the finite eteleiosa would give a second main clause, 'I finished the work'.
ASV 'whom thou gavest me out of the world' is a simple past; ASV distinguishes the perfect in this chapter with 'hast given' (17:12, 17:24), so 'gavest' answers to the aorist edokas.
ASV 'and thou gavest them to me' is again the simple past against ASV's own 'hast given' for the perfect, marking the aorist edokas.
ASV 'all things whatsoever thou hast given me' is the perfect, over against 'gavest' used for the aorist in 17:6 and 17:8.
ASV 'all things ... are from thee' renders a neuter plural subject with 'are' whether the Greek verb stands plural (eisin) or in the regular singular (estin).
ASV 'the words which thou gavest me' is the simple past, ASV's rendering of the aorist as against 'hast given' for the perfect.
ASV 'and these are in the world' renders the near demonstrative houtoi; the pronoun autoi would give 'they'.
ASV 'even as we are' has no 'also'; 'even as' is ASV's rendering of bare kathos here and at 17:16, 17:21, 17:22, and an added kai would show as 'even as we also'.
ASV 'While I was with them, I kept them in thy name' lacks any rendering of en to kosmo, which ASV translates 'in the world' whenever present in this chapter.
ASV 'in thy name which thou hast given me' makes the name the thing given, matching the singular relative ho; the plural ous would make the disciples the gift, 'those whom thou hast given me'.
ASV 'and I guarded them' renders the connective kai, which the omitting reading does not supply.
ASV 'my joy made full in themselves' is reflexive, answering to heautois; autois would give 'in them'.
The readings differ only in the order of ouk eimi and ek tou kosmou; ASV 'even as I am not of the world' follows English order and does not report the Greek sequence.
ASV 'Sanctify them in the truth' has no possessive; the added sou would be rendered 'in thy truth', as ASV renders 'thy word' in the same verse.
The readings differ only in word order within the hina clause; ASV 'that they themselves also may be sanctified' cannot report where osin stood.
Vocative pater and nominative-for-vocative pater are both rendered 'Father'; the ASV shows no difference.
ASV 'that they also may be in us' has no predicate 'one'; the added hen would give 'may be one in us', and ASV does render hen as 'one' in this verse's opening clause.
ASV 'that the world may believe' renders present and aorist subjunctive alike.
ASV 'even as we are one' supplies the copula, as it does at 17:11 ('even as we are') where no verb stands in the Greek; the English therefore does not attest esmen.
ASV 'that they may be perfected into one; that the world may know' joins the two clauses with no 'and', which the added kai would supply.
Vocative Pater and nominative Pater are both rendered 'Father'; the ASV shows no difference.

The ASV note on this verse, 'Greek that which thou hast given me', reports the neuter singular relative ho behind the smoothed 'they also whom thou hast given me'; ous would be the plural the note is correcting.
ASV 'my glory, which thou hast given me' is the perfect, ASV's consistent rendering of dedokas over against 'gavest' for the aorist in 17:6 and 17:8.
Vocative Pater and nominative Pater are both rendered 'Father' in 'O righteous Father'; the ASV shows no difference.
